items.question: How should the guru use the mantra-circle and the disciple's hand in this rite?
premises: The guru should worship the bond-burning mantra-circle with the left hand.
The disciple's body contains the continuum of paths placed within it.
The guru should place that hand of the disciple on the disciple's head.
items.inference: By worshipping the bond-burning mantra-circle and placing the disciple's hand on the head, the guru prepares the disciple's path-filled body for the rite.
uncertainties: The exact referent of taṃ as the disciple's hand or the guru's empowered hand is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The guru should worship the bond-burning circle of mantras with the left hand, then place that hand of the disciple on the head of the disciple whose body contains the whole continuum of paths.

items.question: What placement and touching actions are prescribed and where are they taught?
premises: The guru should place in order on all the disciple's limbs.
The guru should touch the disciple with that very hand.
This is taught in the Dīkṣottara as done with a hand shining with a fall of flames.
items.inference: The ordered placement and touching are authoritative ritual acts performed with the flame-shining hand as taught in the Dīkṣottara.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the Dīkṣottara text is not specified here.
items.plain_english: He should place in order on all the limbs and touch the disciple with that very hand; this is taught in the Dīkṣottara as done with a hand shining with a cascade of flames.

items.question: What status and capacities does the disciple gain through the giving of the Śiva-hand?
premises: By the given Śiva-hand the disciple is made a samaya-initiate.
He gains fitness for knowledge while still living.
He gains union in the Īśvara level.
items.inference: The Śiva-hand confers samaya status, present fitness for knowledge, and future union in the Īśvara level.
uncertainties: Whether sāyujya in the Īśvara level is immediate or post-mortem is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: By the bestowal of the Śiva-hand he is made a samaya-initiate; while still alive he becomes fit for knowledge, and he attains union in the level of Īśvara.

items.question: What alternative ritual circle is taught in the Śrīdevyāthāmala?
premises: The Śrīdevyāthāmala teaches an alternative method.
It uses a circle with an eight-spoked inner trident.
Bhairava is near the navel and Aghora and the other eight form its spokes.
items.inference: The Śrīdevyāthāmala prescribes a trident-circle diagram centered on Bhairava with Aghora and the other eight as its structure.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of sannābhā as 'near the navel' or 'with a good navel' is slightly uncertain.
items.plain_english: But in the Śrīdevyāthāmala it is taught in a circle with an eight-spoked inner trident, with Bhairava at the navel and Aghora and the other eight forming it.

items.question: How is the trident-circle visualized in its outer, rim, and middle parts?
premises: The diagram has an outer lower part and a supreme rim.
It has a middle trident with supreme and lower aspects.
It is visualized as flame-filled, reddish, and fearsome with whirling Mothers and praṇava.
items.inference: The trident-circle is a dynamic, fiery, and fearsome mandala structured by outer, rim, and middle trident zones.
uncertainties: The exact spatial mapping of parā and aparā across rim and middle trident is compressed.
items.plain_english: It is visualized with an outer lower part and a supreme rim, and with a middle trident having supreme and lower aspects, all flame-filled, reddish, and fearsome with whirling Mothers and the praṇava.

rows.grounds: refers to the circle or hand

items.question: What happens when the circle is contemplated in the outer hand and what sign indicates imminent death?
premises: When contemplated and seen in the outer hand, one becomes a samaya-initiate.
Agitation of the bonds and similar signs may appear immediately.
Such signs indicate that the person is about to depart upward.
items.inference: The outer-hand contemplation confers samaya status, but bond-agitation can signal that the subject is near death.
uncertainties: The object of tam in the next verse is anticipated here and remains slightly open.
items.plain_english: When this is contemplated and seen in the outer hand, one becomes a samaya-initiate; but if agitation of the bonds and the like appears at once, that shows the person is about to depart.

items.question: What should be done if the sign shows the person is about to leave the body?
premises: If the person is about to depart, the rite can separate him from the life-breaths.
The guru should worship outside that and cast it on the head.
By this Śiva-hand the person clearly becomes a samaya-initiate.
items.inference: Even in the case of imminent death, the Śiva-hand rite can be applied to confer samaya initiation.
uncertainties: The exact object worshipped outside is not named explicitly.
items.plain_english: If he is about to depart, the guru should worship outside that and cast upon the head what separates him from the life-breaths; by this Śiva-hand he clearly becomes a samaya-initiate.

items.question: What further status and future rite apply to that same initiate?
premises: For that same person there is a future proper separation from level-bonds.
He has the status of a son.
The initiating teachers are to join him to the supreme level.
items.inference: The samaya-initiate may later receive son-status and be joined by teachers to the supreme level through proper bond-separation.
uncertainties: The precise ritual stage named by bhāvividhivat is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: For that same person, in the future proper separation from the bonds of the levels, he has the status of a son, and the initiating teachers are to join him to the supreme level.

items.question: What qualifications and consecration sequence lead to the sādhaka stage?
premises: The same person knows the kinds of mantras.
He knows the truth of recitation, fire-offering, and related practices.
He is consecrated first by the liberation vessel and then by the one named Īśvara.
items.inference: Qualified knowledge and a two-stage consecration prepare the disciple to become a sādhaka.
uncertainties: The exact ritual contents of the Īśvara-named vessel are not detailed here.
items.plain_english: That same person, knowing the kinds of mantras and the truth of recitation, fire-offering, and the rest, is consecrated first with the liberation vessel and then with the one called Īśvara.

items.question: What becomes of the consecrated sādhaka and what further qualities define the initiated in Śiva's teaching?
premises: When consecrated, he becomes a sādhaka.
At the end of enjoyment he attains dissolution in the supreme.
One initiated in Śiva's teaching may also be endowed with further qualities.
items.inference: Consecration establishes sādhaka status leading to final dissolution, while Śiva's teaching also recognizes further qualified initiation.
uncertainties: The verse shifts from the sādhaka to a more qualified initiated person without a fully explicit boundary.
items.plain_english: When consecrated he becomes a sādhaka, and at the end of enjoyment he dissolves into the supreme; endowed with these qualities, one is initiated in the teaching of Śiva.

items.question: What scriptural mastery qualifies someone to be appointed as an ācārya?
premises: He knows the four-part scriptures and is devoted to the eighteen tantras.
He knows the ten tantras and the higher path.
Such a person is appointed as an ācārya.
items.inference: Broad and deep tantric learning across multiple scriptural groups qualifies one for the office of ācārya.
uncertainties: The exact referents of the four-part scriptures and ten tantras are traditional and not specified here.
items.plain_english: One who knows the four-part scriptures, is devoted to the eighteen tantras, and knows the ten tantras and the higher path is appointed as an ācārya.

items.question: How should the best of gurus consecrate an ācārya across the levels?
premises: The joining begins from earth and ends in liberation.
This joining is performed in the consecration rite.
The best of gurus performs it for the ācārya.
items.inference: The ācārya's consecration includes a full ascent-joining from earth to liberation performed by a supreme guru.
uncertainties: The intermediate levels between earth and liberation are implied but not listed.
items.plain_english: In the consecration rite, the best of gurus should perform for the ācārya the joining that begins from earth and ends in liberation.

items.question: What scope of authorization does the samaya-initiate receive according to these statements?
premises: These statements summarize the teaching.
The samaya-initiate is compared to a prince.
He is authorized everywhere in the three stages beginning with son.
items.inference: The samaya-initiate receives broad authorization across the son and related initiatory stages.
uncertainties: The exact three stages included in putrakādipadatraye are not enumerated here.
items.plain_english: By these statements it is said that the samaya-initiate, like a prince, would be authorized everywhere in the three stages beginning with the son stage.

items.question: Under what condition is a son-initiate authorized in teacherhood and when is he not?
premises: A son-initiate may act in teacherhood if his joining is equal.
If the joining is different, he is not authorized in sādhana.
Authorization depends on the level of joining.
items.inference: Teacherly authorization for a son-initiate is conditional on having the same level of joining, not a different one.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of 'equal joining' in practice is not spelled out.
items.plain_english: A son-initiate may be authorized in teacherhood if his joining is equal, but he is not authorized in sādhana when the joining is different.

items.question: Who may serve as ācārya in this tantra and who is excluded?
premises: In this tantra the ācārya must have obtained higher rites through the samaya sequence and beyond.
Buddhists, Vaiṣṇavas, and others are excluded.
The exclusion is absolute.
items.inference: Only one who has progressed through the proper samaya-based sequence may be ācārya in this tantra.
uncertainties: The scope of 'and others' is not specified.
items.plain_english: In this tantra, the ācārya is one who has obtained the higher rites through the sequence beginning with samaya; never a Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava, or the like.

items.question: How does the text return from the digression to the main rite of the Śiva-hand?
premises: The digression has been determined by context.
The main topic is now examined again.
The Śiva-hand rite is performed so that the disciple's bonds are burned away.
items.inference: After the digression, the exposition resumes with the Śiva-hand rite as the means of burning the disciple's bonds.
items.plain_english: Thus what arose by context has been settled, and now the main topic is taken up again: having performed the Śiva-hand rite, by that the disciple's bonds are burned away.

items.question: After burning the bonds, where is the disciple placed through meditative absorption?
premises: The disciple is brought to a state up to rest through meditative yoking.
Then he is placed in the vessel, the weapon-vessel, the fire, and the guru's own self.
The same child-disciple is the object throughout.
items.inference: The rite internalizes and distributes the disciple across key ritual loci through meditation after the burning of bonds.
uncertainties: The exact meditative technique implied by viśrāntiparyantaṃ is not specified.
items.plain_english: Having brought the disciple, through meditative absorption, to the point of rest, the guru then places that child-disciple in the vessel, in the weapon-vessel, in the fire, and in his own self.

items.question: What ritual actions follow the placement of the disciple in the vessels and fire?
premises: The disciple is made to perform prostration.
An offering to the beings and Mothers is cast.
Śaṃkara is worshipped and a bed consecrated by the weapon-mantra is prepared.
items.inference: The rite proceeds through obeisance, offering, worship of Śaṃkara, and preparation of a consecrated bed.
uncertainties: The exact form of the bhūtamātṛbali is not specified.
items.plain_english: He should have the disciple make prostration, then cast an offering to the beings and Mothers; then, having worshipped Śaṃkara, he should prepare a bed consecrated with the weapon-mantra.

items.question: How are the disciple and guru positioned in the heart-wheel and twelve-end during the sleep rite?
premises: The disciple is placed on the consecrated bed with mantras installed.
The guru establishes rest in the disciple's heart-wheel.
The guru then goes to the disciple's twelve-end.
items.inference: The sleep rite aligns the disciple's heart-wheel with the guru's ascent to the twelve-end.
uncertainties: Whether taddvādaśāntagaḥ refers to the disciple's or a shared twelve-end is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: Having placed the disciple on that bed and installed the mantras, the guru establishes rest in the disciple's heart-wheel and then goes to his twelve-end.

items.question: What change occurs in the network of kalās through the arising of the twelve vowels and re-entry?
premises: The net of kalās becomes diminished through the arising of the twelve vowels.
Then, on entry, sixteen kalās are gathered.
This gathering makes the state bright.
items.inference: The practice moves from diminution of kalās to a luminous reconstitution through sixteen gathered kalās.
uncertainties: The technical identity of the kalās here is not fully explained in the verse.
items.plain_english: Through the arising of the twelve vowels the net of kalās becomes diminished; then, on entry, he becomes bright with the sixteen kalās gathered together.

items.question: Where should the guru rest as the full moon of self-consciousness and where should he go afterward?
premises: The guru becomes the full moon of his own consciousness.
He should rest in the heart of the child-disciple until rising.
Then he should go to the twelve-end.
items.inference: The guru stabilizes as full self-consciousness in the disciple's heart and then ascends to the twelve-end.
uncertainties: The exact moment of vyutthāna is not specified.
items.plain_english: As the full moon of his own consciousness, he should rest in the heart of the child-disciple until the rising, and then go to the twelve-end.

items.question: What is the sequence of the sleep rite and what does the sleeping disciple perceive?
premises: The guru should enter the heart-wheel again in this manner.
This constitutes the sequence of the sleep rite.
When sleep has arrived, the disciple perceives the stainless moon and sun.
items.inference: The repeated heart-wheel entry defines the sleep rite and culminates in the disciple's vision of the stainless moon and sun.
uncertainties: The exact number of repetitions is not stated.
items.plain_english: He should enter the heart-wheel again in this way; this is the sequence of the sleep rite. When sleep has come, this disciple perceives the stainless moon and sun.

items.question: How does the disciple perceive the moon and sun in the heart-wheel during this state?
premises: In the heart-wheel the disciple joins together the full and thin moon and sun.
This joining happens forcibly.
He truly sees the light of the forcibly stainless moon and sun.
items.inference: The disciple's heart-wheel vision unites the waxing and waning luminaries into a single stainless light.
uncertainties: The force implied by balāt/haṭha may be yogic or visionary; the verse does not specify.
items.plain_english: In the heart-wheel he forcibly joins together the full and the thin moon and sun, and he truly sees the light of the forcibly stainless moon and sun.

items.question: What kind of dream arises from this vision and what meditation is prescribed for it?
premises: The disciple sees a dream skilled in making future good and other outcomes clear.
Scripture states that one should meditate on the full and the thin.
This meditation occurs in the domain of the twelve.
items.inference: Meditation on the full and thin in the twelve-domain produces a dream that clarifies future auspicious and inauspicious outcomes.
uncertainties: The exact referent of dvādaśagocare is not fully explicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: He sees a dream that clearly reveals future good and other outcomes; and it is taught that, having meditated on the full and the thin in the domain of the twelve, this occurs.
